intelligence.human_view: Some jobs have layers, and one layer good while the others aren't never works. That is the whole law, and the legal pages are the job that proved it: the content layer was summaries, the presentation layer was left-hung plain text — one layer bad and the other bad too, and the whole thing read as a scam. But the deeper truth is that a single good layer can't carry the rest: a beautiful presentation over one-sentence summaries is still not a legal agreement, and airtight drafting in plain unformatted text still reads as not legit to a stranger's eye. The project is one ultimate project, not a stack of separate passes that each get to be "good enough" on their own: the WHOLE thing has to be good — not only good but GREAT — the most elite, ten-star, professional, pro, premium, top-of-the-line, all-star presentation AND outputs AND design AND intelligence put into it. Every layer, or the project isn't done. That is the verdict a round is judged by: not "did my layer pass" but "is the whole thing great in every layer." The letter taught the same lesson from the other side (SN-2980): the picture was fixed and the page was missed — one layer good, the rest not — and it took his eye to catch it. The standard is the whole: presentation, outputs, design, intelligence — all of it, all-star, all at once.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're building the most amazing tower ever — but you make the bottom super strong and beautiful, and then the top is all wobbly and messy! It doesn't work, right? The whole tower has to be great — every single layer, from the bottom to the very top! That's the rule: one ultimate project, and EVERY layer has to be great — the prettiest, the best, ten stars in every single part — or it's not done!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine you're making a beautiful dinner, dear: the main dish is wonderful, but the plates are chipped and the table isn't set and the dessert is burnt! One good layer doesn't make a good dinner, love — the whole thing has to be lovely, every layer of it. It's the same with our work, dear: some jobs have layers, and it's never going to work to say "well, this one layer is good but the others aren't." One ultimate project, love — the WHOLE thing has to be good, not only good but GREAT — the most elite, ten-star, professional, premium, top-of-the-line, all-star in every layer: how it looks, what it does, how it's designed, how smart it is. Every layer, dear, or the project isn't done.
